findings.claim: The README says the attribute is only emitted for targets where it is available, but the guard `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK` is hard-coded. It also omits that generated types other than formatters and resolvers may be undecorated. Nested partial containers emitted by EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces and any other generated helper types (e.g. attribute/helper declarations in the resolver) are not decorated, so the claim 'All generated code' is not fully met. This is a convention/doc accuracy concern.

receipt_plan.detail: Read TransformUtilities.EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces (emits `partial class/struct` wrappers without the attribute) and compare with README wording and REQ-2297 'all generated code'.

findings.claim: The new tests are in a new file whose test class has no `namespace` and uses `Fact`/`Assert` implicitly. Otherwise the tests only check string presence in generated output, not that the generated code compiles on netstandard2.0/.NET Framework targets, which was a derived acceptance criterion.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a test compiling generated output with preprocessor symbols NETSTANDARD2_0 and with NET8_0 and asserting zero diagnostics; the current tests only do string matching.

questions.text: Should ExcludeFromCodeCoverage be emitted unconditionally for all users, or should there be an opt-out setting?
options: Add an opt-out MSBuild/attribute property to disable emission
questions.why_it_matters: The requirement says no setting is needed but one would be fine. If the team wants an opt-out, the unconditional change is incomplete; if not, it is correct as is.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Unconditionally decorate generated formatters (object, string-key, enum, union) and resolvers and their nested helper classes with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage guarded by `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`; no setting; nesting partial wrapper types are left undecorated.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Decorate every generated type, including the partial nesting containers, and add an opt-out setting (e.g. an MSBuild property or attribute option read by the generator) that suppresses emission of the attribute.
